leads.name: 1000jährige Eibe Gutau
leads.why: Verified as Naturdenkmal nd292 in the Land Oberösterreich register, reproduced by de.wikipedia.org 'Liste der Naturdenkmäler im Bezirk Freistadt': a European Yew (Taxus baccata) standing roughly 20m east of the Staudinger farmhouse ('Lehen') in Gutau, Upper Austria, protected since 06.02.1985, at 48.434608N 14.624856E. Second source: monumentaltrees.com's entry for the same tree ('Europäische Eibe auf dem Gelände eines Bauernhauses in Lehen', Freistadt) independently gives the same location (20m east of the Staudinger farmhouse) and adds measurements: stem circumference 1.70m in 1985 rising to 1.90m in 2016 (girth_cm recorded as the circumference figure, not a diameter conversion), height ~11m in Feb 1985. Only one yew Naturdenkmal is listed for the whole Gutau municipality, so this is almost certainly the tree in the Commons photos, though the popular name '1000-year-old yew' does not appear in either official source: it is a local nickname (used on the Boblberg hiking-loop trail this tree sits beside, per a 2023 Naturfreunde hike report placing a photo stop 'bei der 1000 jährigen Eibe' on that route) and the register carries no age field at all. Given a circumference of under 2m, an actual age of a full millennium is very unlikely for this species; leaving age_estimate empty rather than repeating the folk name as fact. Alive: photographed 22 July 2023 (Wikimedia, GLAM on Tour project) and measured as recently as 2016 (monumentaltrees). Access: appears to be a marked stop on a public hiking route (the Boblberg circuit) rather than inside the farmyard itself, but this is inferred from the hike report rather than stated outright by either source; flagging as the one soft point. Clears the bar: alive, two independent sources for species/location, one collectible point, publicly reachable via the trail. Sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_im_Bezirk_Freistadt ; https://www.monumentaltrees.com/de/aut/oberosterreich/freistadt/15713_bauernhausesinlehen/ ; https://holzwiesen.naturfreunde.at/berichte/2023/wanderung-in-gutau-um-den-boblberg/

leads.name: Ahorn Feistererhof, Ramsau am Dachstein
leads.why: Verified as the 'oldest Bergahorn in the Ramsau', standing at 1,170m elevation at the rear of the Feistererhof farm off Feistererweg in Ramsau am Dachstein, Styria. Source 1: ennstalwiki.at's dedicated page 'Ahorn Feistererhof' reports the age from the tree's own on-site information placard, 'vermutlich an die 450 Jahre alt' (presumably around 450 years old) -- repeated here as vaguely as the source gives it, not sharpened. No girth or height figure is given by that source. Source 2 (independent designation record): ennstalwiki.at's district list 'Naturdenkmale im Bezirk Liezen' lists it separately as the official Naturdenkmal 'Ahornbaum Ramsau am Dachstein', object no. 010, confirming protected status distinct from the placard text. Source 3, corroborating location only: the Wikimedia Commons photo (St-Ramsau-Bergahorn-1.jpg, taken 19 July 2017) carries its own geotag of 47°25'40.37"N 13°40'40.19"E (47.427881, 13.677831), matching the lead's supplied coordinates almost exactly, and its own caption independently calls it 'Ältester Bergahorn der Ramsau am Feistererhof ... (Naturdenkmal)'. Two of the three sources live on the same host (ennstalwiki), which is a soft point, but they draw from two different underlying records (an on-site plaque vs. a designation list) and the Commons geotag is fully independent. Alive: photographed 2017, described in present tense as the region's oldest specimen with no indication of loss. Access: reached via Feistererweg at the farm's rear; no source states outright that the public may walk up to it, so treat this as likely but unconfirmed rather than stated plainly -- the farm is a working Bio-Hotel/guesthouse, not obviously fenced off, but I could not find an explicit 'open to visitors' line. Clears the bar on alive/species/location; access is the one point to double check before shipping. Sources: https://www.ennstalwiki.at/wiki/index.php/Ahorn_Feistererhof ; https://www.ennstalwiki.at/wiki/index.php/Naturdenkmale_im_Bezirk_Liezen ; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:St-Ramsau-Bergahorn-1.jpg

leads.name: 1000-jährige Eiche Bad Blumau
leads.why: Well documented tree, locally nicknamed 'die dicke Oachn', standing in Bierbaum an der Safen at the end of the Eichenweg toward Loimeth (municipality of Bad Blumau, Steiermark), on a private plot ('auf einem privaten Grundstück, Ortsende von Bierbaum, nach der kleinen Kapelle' per meinbezirk.at) but treated as a public attraction with marked trails, information signage and guided tours (per meinbezirk.at's Hartberg-Fuerstenfeld article, 'thousands of annual visitors'). Species and measurements from baumkunde.de's tree register (dendrology enthusiast database, last visited/measured 09.08.2018): Stiel-Eiche/Pedunculate Oak (Quercus robur), girth 8.75m (875cm) at that visit, height 30m, coordinates N47 6.32538' E16 2.94798' (converted: 47.105423, 16.049133), status 'vital' and 'öffentlich zugänglich' (publicly accessible). AGE IS DISPUTED, both figures kept rather than one picked: baumkunde.de gives 500-600 years as its own measurement-based estimate and explicitly flags this as contradicting the popular name; meinbezirk.at's Hartberg-Fuerstenfeld piece instead states 'Experten bestaetigen: rund 1.000 Jahre alt' and repeats the legend that it was 'allegedly planted around the year 1020'. No source states which experts or method reached the 1000-year figure, so it reads as the same unverified local tradition rather than an independent dendrological measurement; baumkunde's girth-based figure is more likely the sounder one but I am not picking a winner. Alive: meinbezirk (graz community edition) reports a lightning strike in the 1970s that was clumsily filled with concrete, causing decay, and a restoration in 1989 by tree surgeon Manfred Saller funded by a donation from Heidi Horten, after which 'the oldest oak in Europe shines again in full vitality'; baumkunde's 2018 visit independently confirms 'vital' condition. Clears the bar: alive and vital as of the two most recent checks (1989 restoration outcome, 2018 measurement), two independent sources for species/age/location that actually disagree on age (flagged rather than resolved), one collectible point, publicly reachable despite private ownership of the plot. Sources: https://www.baumkunde.de/baumregister/1309-tausendjaehrige_eiche_in_bad_blumau/ ; https://www.meinbezirk.at/hartberg-fuerstenfeld/c-lokales/die-1000-jaehrige-eiche-von-bierbaum_a7441969 ; https://www.meinbezirk.at/graz/c-regionauten-community/die-1000-jaehrige-eiche-in-bierbaum-gemeinde-bad-blumau_a5050954
